column2: I/O port resource may not be assigned to all

column1: the PCI devices since it is limited (to 64KB on Intel Architecture[1])
and it may also be fragmented (I/O base register of PCI-to-PCI bridge
will usually be aligned to a 4KB boundary[2]).
If no I/O port resource is assigned to devices
work.
[1] Some machines support 64KB I/O port space per PCI segment.
[2] Some P2P bridges support optional 1KB aligned I/O base.
Therefore
column2: I made a patch for MegaRAID SAS driver to make PCI legacy

column1: I/O port free.  I have also tested the patch and it had no problem.
The way to make PCI legacy I/O port free is the same as Fusion-MPT
driver's and it has been merged into 2.6.30.4.
This has already been fixed in e1000 and lpfc.
As a result of the above
column2: the driver can handle its device even when

column1: there are a huge number of PCI devices being used on the system and no
